transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… I guess I’m here because I’ve been having a harder time thinking clearly at work. It’s probably not as bad as I’m making it sound, but my brain kind of… stalls out. Like I’ll have a test report open, or even just a simple CAD note, and I’ll sit there for an hour not able to decide what the next sentence should be, or which checkbox to mark. I know that sounds small, but it’s been getting in the way, and I thought I should probably talk to someone.
How long have you been experiencing this difficulty with thinking clearly at work?

Um… it’s been a little over a year, I think. It started after I got moved into the prototype-testing role — about a year and a month ago. I mean, it wasn’t all at once or anything, but that’s when I started noticing it.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time since you started experiencing these difficulties with thinking clearly at work?

I’m… not sure I’d say sad most of the time, exactly. I mean, I’ve been stressed and kind of discouraged about work, but I don’t know if that counts as “down.” Maybe sometimes, but I don’t want to overstate it.
Have you been enjoying things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with friends and family, about as much as you always have?

Not really, I guess. I mean, I still try to do some of those things, so it’s not like I’ve completely stopped. But my little printer for miniatures has had the same half-finished figure sitting there for months. And even things like yoga or going for a walk in the woods… they kind of feel like another task I’m supposed to do, not something I actually want to do. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you feel like you've lost interest in things that used to bring you pleasure?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but things I used to actually look forward to just don’t feel the same. Like, my miniatures printer has had the same half-finished figure sitting there for months, and even yoga or walking in the woods feels more like something I’m supposed to check off than something I really want to do. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over the past year?

Not that I’ve really noticed. I mean, my clothes seem to fit about the same, so I don’t think there’s been anything significant. I don’t weigh myself very regularly, though, so… I might not be the best judge.
Have you been having any problems with your sleep?

Um… I don’t know, maybe a little, but I haven’t really been tracking it closely. Some nights are better than others. I guess I wouldn’t want to call it a major problem unless that’s what you mean? I can pay more attention to it if that would help.
Have you been feeling more tired than usual?
I’m not totally sure. I mean, I get tired like anyone does, especially after work, but I haven’t really been keeping track of whether it’s more than usual. Maybe a bit? I don’t want to overstate it.
Have you been feeling guilty about anything in particular lately?

Um… yeah, a little. I mean, maybe more than a little, I guess. I keep thinking about small mistakes I’ve made at the lab, things that probably other people would just fix and move on from, but I replay them over and over.

And then it turns into this feeling like I’m not just bad at the job, but… bad as a person. Like if something happens because of it, I deserve it. I know that probably sounds dramatic, sorry. I’m trying to answer honestly.
Have you been feeling hopeless about the future?

I don’t know… I wouldn’t say hopeless, exactly. I mean, I have days where it’s hard to picture things getting much better, but maybe everyone feels that way sometimes. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. I guess I’m not really sure how to answer that correctly.
Have you been feeling worthless?

I guess… yes, sometimes. I don’t want to sound like I’m being overly dramatic, but I keep replaying these tiny mistakes from the lab, and it turns into me thinking I’m not just bad at the job, I’m just… bad. Like as a person. And then I feel like whatever consequences come from it, I probably deserve them. Does that make sense?
Do you still enjoy doing things that normally bring you pleasure, or has that changed recently?

Yeah… it’s changed some. I don’t want to make it sound like I’ve stopped everything completely, but things I usually like just feel kind of… flat, I guess.

Like my printer for miniatures has had the same half-finished figure sitting there for months, and I keep meaning to go back to it, but I just don’t. And even yoga or walking in the woods—things that usually help—feel more like another task I’m supposed to do than something I actually want to do. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you been experiencing these feelings of worthlessness and guilt nearly every day?

Nearly every day… I think so, yes. I don’t want to overstate it, but it’s kind of become this loop where I replay small mistakes from the lab and then it turns into, like, “I’m not just bad at this job, I’m bad as a person.” And then I feel like I deserve whatever happens because of it. Is that… the kind of guilt you mean?
How many days a week would you say you've been feeling down or depressed?

Um… I’m not totally sure I’ve been keeping track that clearly. It’s not like I mark it on a calendar or anything.

Maybe… several days? I don’t want to guess wrong. Some weeks it feels like more than others, but I’m not sure I could give you an exact number. Is it okay if I say it feels frequent, but I don’t know the exact days?
Would you say your feelings of depression are mild, moderate, or severe most of the time?

I’d probably say… moderate? I mean, I can still get through some things, so I don’t want to call it severe if that sounds like I’m completely unable to function. But it’s more than mild, I think. It’s there most of the time and it takes effort to push through. Does moderate sound right for that?
Are there any activities that you still enjoy and look forward to?

I mean… there are things I used to enjoy, but I don’t really look forward to them the same way. My miniature printer has just been sitting there with the same half-finished figure for months, which is kind of embarrassing.

Even things that should be easy, like yoga or going for a walk in the woods, feel more like another task I’m supposed to do than something I actually want to do. I can still try sometimes, but it doesn’t feel… enjoyable exactly. Is that what you mean?
Have you been having any thoughts about hurting yourself?

Um… I don’t think I want to hurt myself exactly. Or I don’t want to say it that way if that sounds too dramatic.

But… on my commute sometimes I catch myself thinking it would be easier if I just didn’t arrive anywhere. And a couple times the thought of steering off the road has come up, which scares me enough that I grip the wheel really hard or pull over. I’m not trying to do anything, but… it does happen. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
How long do these periods of feeling down or depressed usually last?

It’s been… longer than I’d like to admit, I guess. I think it really started after I was moved into the prototype-testing role at work, and that was about a year and a month ago now.

It’s not like every single minute is exactly the same, but the overall down feeling has been there since then. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Have you had periods of feeling down or depressed like this before in your life?

I’m not totally sure. I mean, I’ve had rough patches before, like anyone, especially when things were stressful, but I don’t know that it was… like this.

I don’t want to overstate it. I guess this feels more persistent than what I remember before. Does that make sense?
Do you find that your feelings of depression tend to follow a certain pattern throughout the year?

I don’t think I’ve noticed a yearly pattern, no. Like, I can’t say it gets worse every winter or better in the summer or anything that clear.

I might just not be paying attention to it the right way, though. Should I be looking for something specific?
